title: Decoding Moiré Patterns of Small, Embedded SiC Nanoparticles in Si with Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Retrieval of atomic structure and defects in embedded nanoparticles can be difficult, or even impossible, for sparsely distributed particles with sizes below typical sample thicknesses. Moiré patterns, typically used to determine structural information [1] indirectly, are ineffective when particles are small (< 10 nm) and inhomogeneous. Moreover, prior information about the crystal structures present and their possible orientations is often required to characterize atomic structure conclusively. In this presentation, we consider silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles embedded in a Si matrix, where understanding Moiré patterns is challenging yet crucial to understanding and engineering their quantum properties.
